meta.titre: Trade Unions in French Cameroon: from the war years to the Trusteeship
meta.sous_theme: Workers' organisations and political change in French Cameroon

sections.contenu_markdown: Imagine a dock worker in Douala in the early 1940s. He works long hours, may be sent to forced labour and has no union to speak for him. After the Second World War, laws changed and workers began to organise. Trade unions then became a training ground for people who later led political parties. Examiners ask short questions on the war, the unions and the policies removed, and longer questions on the importance of unions. This course gives you the facts and a method.

items: A trade union is an organisation of workers that defends their pay and conditions.
Forced labour obliged Africans to work without choice and often without proper pay.
Trusteeship was the system of UN supervision that replaced the League mandates after 1945.

sections.titre: Workers and unions in French Cameroon after 1939
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Before the unions

Under French rule Africans lived under harsh policies. The indigenat (native code) allowed administrators to punish Africans without a proper trial, forced labour took men away from their farms, and taxes were heavy. African workers could not freely form unions.

### The war and its effects

The Second World War, 1939 to 1945, changed the situation. Cameroon supported the Free French in 1940. After the war France promised reforms, and at the Brazzaville Conference of 1944 it considered a new relationship with its African territories. In the years after the war, forced labour and the indigenat were abolished. Taxes, however, did not disappear.

### Unions

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1944 | The Union of Confederated Trade Unions of Cameroon (USCC) was formed, linked to a French union federation |
| 1946 | The Trusteeship period began, with France administering Cameroon for the United Nations |
| Later 1940s and 1950s | More unions appeared and workers organised in several trades |

### What unions did

Unions asked for better wages and working conditions and for equal treatment of workers. They organised meetings and strikes. They also taught Africans to organise, speak in public and negotiate. Some future nationalist leaders, among them Ruben Um Nyobè, who later led the UPC, took part in the union movement.

### Limits

The colonial authorities watched unions closely and often restricted their action. Many union members joined the political struggle, so the line between unions and nationalist parties was not always clear.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for a name, a year or a number of items
variantes.contenu_markdown: The war of 1939 to 1945 is the Second World War. A union formed before 1945 is the USCC (1944). Two policies removed after the war: forced labour and the indigenat. The Trusteeship period began in 1946. Write exactly what is requested and keep to the number of items.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked about contribution to nationalism or to workers
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give two or three points: they defended workers, they trained leaders, they joined the demand for change. Support each point with a fact.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question connects unions and parties
variantes.contenu_markdown: Explain that unions gave Africans organising experience that nationalist parties later used, and that union leaders and political leaders sometimes were the same people.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the end of the Second World War changed the position of African workers in French Cameroon. [8 marks]

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: After the Second World War, African workers in French Cameroon gained more freedom. Before the war, forced labour and the indigenat gave the colonial administration great power over them, and unions were not free. After the war, forced labour and the indigenat were abolished, workers could organise in unions, and the Trusteeship period began in 1946. Unions such as the USCC asked for better pay and conditions. In conclusion, the position of workers improved, although taxes remained and the authorities still watched union activity.

items.erreur_markdown: Confusing the USCC with the UPC.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing about unions in British Cameroons.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the war of 1939 to 1945 and give the year in which the Trusteeship period began in French Cameroon.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each. **Second World War; 1946.**

items.enonce_markdown: Give two things that trade unions in French Cameroon asked for and explain one.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for two demands, such as higher wages, better working conditions or fair treatment. **The explanation must say why the demand mattered, for example low wages made life hard.**

items.enonce_markdown: Assess the contribution of trade unions to the growth of nationalism in French Cameroon. [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for both sides. Contribution: defended workers, taught organisation and public speaking, produced leaders, joined demands for change. Limits: restricted by authorities, union members and political activists overlapped. **Judgement: unions were important but worked alongside political parties.**

items_markdown: The war of 1939 to 1945 was the Second World War.
The USCC, formed in 1944, is a union that you can name.
Forced labour and the indigenat were removed after the war; taxes remained.
Unions asked for better pay and conditions and trained leaders.
Distinguish unions from political parties such as the UPC.
